text: NEXUS is Hasan Ali Rajab's independent RAG and product-analytics project. Its public sandbox answers only from curated public project case studies, using a fixed sample tenant and retrieval role. Owner keys, ingestion, private documents and enterprise actions are not available to guests. SQL analytics defines ordered session-start, question-start and completed-answer funnels, user-level A/B inference, cohort retention, latency and failure guardrails. The experiment dataset contains 800 simulated subjects assigned independently to A and B; simulated uplift is not customer or revenue impact. Real visitor analytics is separate, opt-in, aggregated and excludes owner-authenticated QA sessions.

The Telecom project scanned 200,908,858 raw Telecom Italia country-code rows. It selected 618,755 source rows for 30 cells across 38 days, producing 27,360 hourly modelling rows. Four purged rolling-origin folds compare LightGBM with a seasonal-naive baseline. One-hour MAE falls 21.68%; the paired 24-hour block-bootstrap interval excludes zero. The 24-hour point gain is 4.19%, but its interval includes zero, so gains are concentrated at short horizons. Held-out anomaly evaluation uses 24 injected events, with 20 true positives, 16 false positives and 4 false negatives: event F1 0.667, recall 0.833. Injected anomalies are simulated labels on real traffic. Capacity is a training-period 95th-percentile proxy, not operator-engineered capacity. SQL marts and interactive dashboards support demand review, error analysis and capacity scenarios.

SentinelIQ's public model sandbox scores simulated system metrics without creating private alerts. Its separate Isolation Forest benchmark uses a committed synthetic stream of 605 records, partitioned in time into 363 training, 121 validation and 121 test records. The test has 9 anomalous records: 8 true positives, 0 false positives, 1 false negative and 112 true negatives. Record-level F1 is 0.941 and recall 0.889. Threshold selection uses validation labels and remains frozen for the test. This small synthetic benchmark does not establish real incident performance and does not evaluate BERT, the autoencoder or the deployed ensemble. Host and anomaly-type breakdowns support error analysis, including a missed synthetic memory-leak record.
